text:
maria: Ran an overnight cross-device probe comparing kernel picks and end-to-end p99s across small GPUs (L4/T4/A10) and large (A100/H100). TL;DR: small devices prefer the small-kernel hotpath for seqlen<=64; large devices win with the fused/large-kernel path at >=128. Also saw KV-cache eviction thrash on L4 at higher batch sizes. Posting the summarized numbers and a few notes.

perf-bot: perf-probe/2478765432 completed — results uploaded to /mnt/perf/probes/2478765432 (runs: l4,t4,a10,a100,h100).

nate: Nice — can you paste the kernel selection map you observed? names like "small_attn_v1" vs "fused_attn_v3" are enough.

maria: Sure, output from the selector (trimmed):
```
device  | seqlen_range | chosen_kernel      | avg_rt_ms (p50/p95/p99) | batch_cap
L4      | 1-64         | small_attn_v1      | 12/18/26                | 8
T4      | 1-64         | small_attn_v1      | 14/21/30                | 8
A10     | 1-96         | small_attn_v2      | 10/15/22                | 16
A100    | 1-128        | fused_attn_v3      | 8/11/14                 | 32
H100    | 1-512        | fused_attn_v4      | 6/9/12                  | 64
```
Notes: L4/T4 switch point looked around 64 tokens; A10 sits in between. Batch cap on L4 caused KV eviction when concurrent cached prefixes > ~4k tokens.

chen: Interesting. For L4 the small_attn_v1 path is okay but we should avoid batch>4 when there are concurrent KV-resident prefixes — that eviction thrash is killing p99. Could we add a cheap heuristic: if avg_cached_prefix_tokens > 2k then reduce batch_cap to 4?

nate: +1. Also for A10 we probably want the seqlen autopick border at 96 (not 128). I saw small_attn_v2 hold up until 96 then fused wins. Could be quantization kernel differences (int8 path on A10 behaves differently).

maria: Agreed. Draft preset I'm thinking:
```
preset: arch-gap-lowmem-v1
rules:
  - device_family: [L4, T4]
    seqlen_threshold: 64
    prefer_kernel: small_attn_v1
    batch_cap: 4 when avg_cached_prefix_tokens > 2000 else 8
    warmup_requests: 4
  - device_family: [A10]
    seqlen_threshold: 96
    prefer_kernel: small_attn_v2
    batch_cap: 16
    warmup_requests: 2
  - device_family: [A100, H100]
    seqlen_threshold: 128
    prefer_kernel: fused_attn_v3
    batch_cap: 32
    warmup_requests: 1
fallback_policy: fall back to small_attn_v1 on OOM or >10% latency regression
```
I'd like to canary this on staging for traffic shapes that mimic long prefix chat workloads.

perf-bot: note: the A10 run used int8-quant kernels; fused_attn_v3 used float16 kernels on A100. Perf comparisons are apples->oranges unless we normalize for precision.

chen: Good catch from perf-bot. We should include a precision field in selector metadata and maybe a normalization factor in the regen reports so the autotuner doesn't prefer float16 just because it's faster.

nate: Another gotcha: KV cache eviction patterns differ — L4 memory fragmentation leads to >10% variance on repeated runs. Suggest we add a short random jitter to batch coalescing on L4 to avoid pathological alignment.

maria: Action items: 1) I'll add the preset to git in /infra/presets/arch-gap-lowmem-v1.yaml and enable canary for the staging pool (id: stg-infer-3). 2) Add precision tag to kernel metadata and include a normalize flag in perf probe pipeline. 3) Implement the "reduce batch_cap when cached_prefix > X" heuristic for L4/T4. I'll kick off a canary run tonight and drop results in this thread. ETA tomorrow AM.

chen: :thumbsup: Also add a regression-guard in rollout code: if avg p99 increases >5% after deploy, auto-roll back the preset.

maria: Will do. Raw probe command I ran:
```
kernelselector --probe --devices L4,T4,A10,A100,H100 \
  --seqlens 16,32,64,96,128,256 --batch-sizes 1,2,4,8,16,32 \
  --workload chat-prefix-heavy --out /mnt/perf/probes/2478765432
```
Logs: /mnt/perf/probes/2478765432/raw.log (attached).

nate: Great. After canary, let's also run a short regression harness with our eval prompts to ensure quality parity (int8 vs fp16).

maria: Yep — will include eval set. Thanks folks.
